quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When someone passes you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver is dangerous and increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which surface is potentially slippery?

options.text: A gravel road
A paved driveway
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Gravel roads have poor traction. Other slippery surfaces include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, lane markings, and steel plates.

questions.question: What can a plastic face shield protect you from?

options.text: Noise
Dust
Glare

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your face during crashes and from everyday hazards like pebbles thrown by other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: Which brake is stronger on a motorcycle?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
Both brakes are equally strong.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Experienced riders use "SIPDE" to stay aware. What does the "P" stand for?

options.text: Pass
Predict
Potential
Problem

questions.correctAnswerText: Predict
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process riders use to judge situations and take action. The letters stand for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: How should riders generally position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In a single line.
In pairs.
In a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close together while keeping safe distance around each rider. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving over bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross faster.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Keep steady speed and go straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep steady speed and go straight across.
questions.explanation: Maintain a steady speed and ride straight across bridge gratings. Do not zigzag, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers about merging traffic ahead.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or drab colors while riding.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if safe. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers that you are near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping when they don't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping when they don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to warn other drivers when you slow down or stop unexpectedly. This is especially important before making a sharp, fast turn off a high-speed road. Always flash your brake light when slowing down in places where drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: Reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help make motorcycle riders more visible.
Do not increase a motorcycle rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help make motorcycle riders more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: Stopping in a turn is difficult because:

options.text: The bike's grip on the road decreases when it is leaning.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike's grip on the road decreases when it is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be very careful. When the motorcycle leans to turn, some of its grip is used for the turn. This means less grip is available for stopping.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get the best grip.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride as fast as you would during the day.
Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride more slowly at night, especially on roads you don't know well. Slower speeds give you more time to spot and avoid hazards when you cannot see as far ahead.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency.
Should be used together with the rear brake.
Is unsafe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you see a hazard in the road, do not:

options.text: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
Change your speed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Alert other drivers to your presence by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed to match the situation. Change your lane position or direction of travel as needed.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet whenever you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When carrying a load, it should be:

options.text: Secured as high as possible.
Secured as low as possible.
Secured on a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Secure loads as low as possible to keep the motorcycle balanced properly.

questions.question: When another rider is passing you, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding close to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding too far away may cause the other driver to cut back into your lane unsafely.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle jacket and pants fit?

options.text: Loosely, so wind can flow through the fabric.
Snugly enough to prevent flapping in the wind.
Tightly, so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly enough to prevent flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snug enough to prevent wind flapping, but loose enough to allow free movement.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: They show everything behind you perfectly.
They do not show your blind spots.
You should only use them when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Look far ahead on the road.
Avoid busy traffic areas.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Always scan the road far ahead of you. This helps you spot hazards early and react to them safely before you reach them.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.
